title: Dock scheduling outage at Harbour Freight

messages.text: The dock scheduling service at Harbour Freight fell over again at 04:12 and the night shift could not dispatch the 05:00 manifest.
That is the second failure this month at the same hour, which points at something scheduled rather than load. What does the service log say immediately before it stops responding?
It holds a database connection open while it polls S3 for the manifest object, and when the key is missing it retries forever instead of failing.
So the missing key is the trigger and the retry is the amplifier. A poll loop that cannot distinguish absent from delayed will never terminate.
The retry loop is the connection exhaustion: about 40 attempts a second, each one grabbing a pooled connection and never releasing it.
Then the pool empties in under a minute and everything behind it queues. Capping attempts and closing the connection per attempt fixes the amplification, not just the symptom.
We renamed the monitoring stack to Lighthouse last quarter, so the alerts now come from lighthouse-dock rather than the old service name, which confused the on-call rota.
Alert source renames are worth a line in the runbook, the rota reads the sender not the payload. Update the escalation names in the same change.
I want the manifest job to fail fast after three attempts and push the batch to a dead-letter queue that the ops team actually watches.
Three attempts then dead-letter is the right shape. The queue only works if someone owns it, so put the drain on the same rota as the alerts.
The ferry manifests themselves are only about 200 rows a day, so volume was never the problem. It was entirely the retry behaviour.
Two hundred rows a day is nothing. Worth saying that out loud in the note, because it closes off the obvious wrong conclusion about scale.
Ticket is DOCK-4471 and the client wants a post-incident note by Friday.
DOCK-4471 noted. The note should carry the timeline, the retry amplification, and the three changes: attempt cap, dead-letter queue, and the alert rename.
The 05:00 dispatch is automated from the manifest now, so the night shift only confirms it rather than keying it in.
